title: [fix] Dequantize int8 model2vec embeddings in StaticEmbedding
body:
Closes #4386

model2vec's quantize_to="int8" stores integer embeddings, which model2vec averages in float32. StaticEmbedding._fold_model2vec_weights only promoted the embeddings to float32 when per-token weights were present, so a plain int8 model reached nn.EmbeddingBag.from_pretrained as int8 and failed with "Only Tensors of floating point and complex dtype can require gradients". This affected SentenceTransformer(path) on a saved int8 model2vec model, StaticEmbedding.from_model2vec, and StaticEmbedding.from_distillation(..., quantize_to="int8").

Change: in _fold_model2vec_weights, cast non-floating-point embeddings to float32 before folding, matching model2vec. Float embeddings, mapping and weights are handled as before. All three loading paths go through this helper.

Tests:
- New test_load_model2vec_int8_embeddings saves an int8 "embeddings" tensor, loads it with StaticEmbedding.load, and checks the weights are float32 and the outputs are the float means. It fails on main with the RuntimeError above.
- pytest tests/sentence_transformer/modules/test_static_embedding.py: 23 passed, 1 skipped; 3 tests that download models from the Hub (or need PIL) could not run in my offline environment and fail the same way on main.
- The reproduction from the issue now loads and matches StaticModel.encode exactly; from_distillation(quantize_to="int8") on a tiny local BERT now returns float32 weights.
- ruff check, ruff format --check and typos pass on the changed files.

Disclosure: found, reproduced and the draft fix tested locally with the help of an AI coding agent (Claude Code); reviewed before filing.

title: [feat] Add optional NumPy output to cos_sim
body:
Resolves #2513

Hello!

## Pull Request overview
* Add an opt-in `convert_to_numpy` flag to `util.cos_sim`, so NumPy users can get a NumPy score matrix back.

## Details
In #2513, Tom preferred a flag over changing the return type ("A flag might be a better solution"), since returning NumPy for NumPy inputs could break existing code. The reporter proposed the `convert_to_numpy` name, which `encode` already uses.

- `cos_sim(a, b, convert_to_numpy=True)` returns the same matrix as a NumPy array, detached from autograd and moved to CPU, through the existing `_tensor_to_numpy` helper (bfloat16 becomes float32).
- The default is `False`, so the return type, device and gradients are unchanged. `typing.overload`s keep `cos_sim(a, b)` typed as returning a `Tensor`.
- The similarity reference page gets a short example.

I kept the scope to `cos_sim`. Should `dot_score`, `manhattan_sim`, `euclidean_sim` and the pairwise variants get the same flag? I'm happy to add that here or in a follow-up.

## Tests
- `tests/util/test_similarity.py`: values and shapes for list, ndarray and tensor inputs; float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 inputs; a detached result for inputs that require grad; sparse inputs; and the default still returns a tensor with gradients.
- `tests/sentence_transformer/test_compute_embeddings.py`: `encode(..., convert_to_numpy=True)` followed by `cos_sim(..., convert_to_numpy=True)` matches scikit-learn's `cosine_similarity`.

title: [fix] Always evaluate `main_similarity` when `similarity_fn_names` omits it
body:
When `similarity_fn_names` (or `score_functions` for IR) is given explicitly and doesn't contain the main similarity, the evaluator still names a `primary_metric` for the main similarity, but never computes it. Anything that reads the primary metric then fails: `SequentialEvaluator` and the trainer raise `KeyError`. #4363 fixed this for IR when `score_functions` is unset; the explicit-list case remained, in IR and in the STS and triplet evaluators. I found it by code analysis, not in use.

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from sentence_transformers.base.evaluation import SequentialEvaluator
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.evaluation import EmbeddingSimilarityEvaluator

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors")
evaluator = EmbeddingSimilarityEvaluator(
    ["a cat sits on the mat", "a man is playing guitar", "the sky is blue"],
    ["a kitten rests on a rug", "someone plays an instrument", "grass is green"],
    [0.9, 0.7, 0.2],
    main_similarity="dot",
    similarity_fn_names=["cosine"],
    name="sts",
)
SequentialEvaluator([evaluator])(model)
```

- `main`: `KeyError: 'sts_spearman_dot'` (the results only have the cosine metrics). `TripletEvaluator(main_similarity_function="dot", similarity_fn_names=["cosine"])` fails the same way, and `InformationRetrievalEvaluator(score_functions={"cosine": cos_sim}, main_score_function="dot")` returns results without its primary metric.
- With this PR: the STS and triplet evaluators also compute the main similarity, and IR raises a clear `ValueError` at construction.

Realistic case: picking a main similarity for model selection (`metric_for_best_model`) while listing the similarity functions to report, e.g. `main_similarity="dot"` with `similarity_fn_names=["cosine"]`.

**Change:**
- `EmbeddingSimilarityEvaluator` and `TripletEvaluator` append the main similarity to `similarity_fn_names` when it's missing (previously only when the list was empty). The user's order is kept; the main function is added at the end. Side effect: the evaluator now reports one more function, so the `*_max` metrics and the CSV columns include it.
- `InformationRetrievalEvaluator` and `NanoBEIREvaluator` raise a `ValueError` at construction when an explicit `score_functions` doesn't contain `main_score_function`, through a shared `validate_main_score_function` helper. NanoBEIR checks before loading any dataset. I chose raising over appending here because `score_functions` values are arbitrary callables (and the multi-vector variants bind `chunk_elements`), so silently adding a built-in function could score with the wrong one. Happy to switch to appending if you prefer. The sparse and multi-vector variants inherit both checks; their docstrings now say `main_score_function` must be a key of `score_functions`.

**Tests:**
- `test_embedding_similarity_evaluator.py` and `test_triplet_evaluator.py`: the main similarity is evaluated with an explicit list (one and two functions).
- `test_information_retrieval_evaluator.py`: raises when the main function is missing; accepted when present.
- `test_nanobeir_evaluator.py`: raises before any dataset is loaded.
- All but the "accepted when present" guard fail on `main` and pass with the fix.

- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation tests/sparse_encoder/evaluation tests/multi_vector_encoder/evaluation`: 177 passed, 5 skipped
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`: pass

Not included: `EmbeddingSimilarityEvaluator` silently skips unknown names such as `"cos"`, and the CSV write then fails. `TripletEvaluator` already validates names; I can send that separately.

**AI disclosure:** I used Claude Code (Anthropic) to trace the primary-metric handling across these evaluators, write the reproducer, and draft the tests and this description. I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: [fix] Raise a clear error when RerankingEvaluator has no usable samples
body:
### Problem

`RerankingEvaluator` drops every sample that doesn't have both a positive and a negative document. When that leaves no samples, nothing complains until evaluation, which then crashes with an error that doesn't point at the cause:

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.evaluation import RerankingEvaluator

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors")
evaluator = RerankingEvaluator([{"query": "q", "positive": ["a"], "negative": []}])
evaluator(model)
# ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity
```

`SparseRerankingEvaluator` fails the same way with `RuntimeError: stack expects a non-empty TensorList`, and `MultiVectorRerankingEvaluator` with the numpy error above.

### Cause

After filtering, `self.samples` can be empty. `__call__` then reaches the dataset stats log line, which runs `np.min` / `np.max` over empty lists.

### Fix

Raise a `ValueError` in the constructor right after the filtering step when no samples are left:

```
RerankingEvaluator needs at least one sample with at least one positive and one negative document.
```

`SparseRerankingEvaluator` and `MultiVectorRerankingEvaluator` call this constructor, so they get the same error. An evaluator with at least one usable sample behaves exactly as before. `CrossEncoderRerankingEvaluator` is a separate class that already handles these samples, so it's unchanged.

### Validation

- New `test_reranking_evaluator_without_valid_samples_raises` (an empty list, positives only, negatives only). It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- Ran positive-only, negative-only and mixed samples through all four reranking evaluators: the three bi-encoder ones now raise the new error, and mixed samples and `CrossEncoderRerankingEvaluator` give the same results as before.
- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation tests/sparse_encoder/evaluation tests/multi_vector_encoder/evaluation -q -n 6`: 173 passed, 5 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files sentence_transformers/sentence_transformer/evaluation/reranking.py tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation/test_reranking_evaluator.py`: ruff check, ruff format and typos passed.

Versions: sentence-transformers 6.4.0.dev0 (main @ 688fd663), transformers 5.22.1, torch 2.15.0+cpu, Python 3.12.2, Windows 11.

### AI assistance

I used Claude Code to find the bug, write the fix and the regression test, and draft this description.

title: [fix] Accept single vectors in pairwise_angle_sim
body:
### Problem

`pairwise_angle_sim` raises `IndexError: tuple index out of range` for a pair of 1D vectors, while every other `pairwise_*` similarity accepts them and returns a scalar:

```python
import torch
from sentence_transformers.util import pairwise_angle_sim, pairwise_cos_sim

a, b = torch.randn(4), torch.randn(4)
pairwise_cos_sim(a, b)    # tensor(...)
pairwise_angle_sim(a, b)  # IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

### Cause

It hardcodes the embedding axis as `1` (`x.shape[1]`, and `dim=1` in `normalize`, `sum` and `chunk`). A 1D input has no axis 1. The sibling pairwise functions use the last axis.

### Fix

Use the last axis (`shape[-1]`, `dim=-1`). For the usual `(batch, dim)` input that is the same axis, so batched results are unchanged.

### Validation

- New `test_pairwise_angle_sim_single_vectors` (even and odd embedding dimensions, since odd ones take the padding path): checks each 1D score matches that row of the batched result and has the same `()` shape as `pairwise_cos_sim`. It fails on `main` with the `IndexError` above and passes with this change.
- `pytest tests/util/test_similarity.py -q`: 154 passed, 9 skipped.
- `pytest tests/util/test_similarity.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses tests/sparse_encoder/losses -q -k "angle or similarity"` (covers `AnglELoss` and `SparseAnglELoss`): 208 passed, 33 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files sentence_transformers/util/similarity.py tests/util/test_similarity.py`: ruff check, ruff format and typos passed.

Versions: sentence-transformers 6.4.0.dev0 (main @ 688fd663), transformers 5.22.1, torch 2.15.0+cpu, Python 3.12.2, Windows 11.

title: [fix] Strip Unicode punctuation in WhitespaceTokenizer and PhraseTokenizer
body:
Resolves #4378

## Problem

Both tokenizers strip punctuation with `token.strip(string.punctuation)`, which is ASCII only. A word followed by non-ASCII punctuation, such as the Arabic comma in `القاهرة،`, is not found in the vocabulary and is silently dropped.

## Change

- Add a private helper `_strip_punctuation` in `tokenizer/word.py` that strips leading and trailing characters that are in `string.punctuation` or in a Unicode punctuation category (`P*`).
- Use it in `WhitespaceTokenizer.tokenize` and `PhraseTokenizer.tokenize`.

ASCII behaviour is unchanged: symbols in `string.punctuation` that are not Unicode punctuation (e.g. `$`, `+`) are still stripped. Combining marks (e.g. Arabic diacritics) are not stripped.

## Not changed

`PhraseTokenizer` lowercases a token before stripping punctuation, so `Cairo。` with a cased vocabulary entry `Cairo` still misses. That ordering is older behaviour and is left alone to keep this PR small.

## Validation

- New `tests/sentence_transformer/modules/test_tokenizer.py`: 16 cases across both tokenizers (Arabic comma, question mark and semicolon, guillemets, CJK full stop, ASCII symbols, punctuation only). On `main` 9 fail; with the fix all pass.
- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/modules`: 310 passed, 159 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_static_embedding.py::test_unsupported_modality`, which needs Pillow and fails the same way on `main` in my environment.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass.

Claude Code helped with the investigation, the patch and the tests. I reviewed every line and ran the tests myself.

title: Fix upstream gradient scaling for trainable cached-loss heads
body:
A trainable similarity module currently accumulates gradients inside `CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss.forward()`. The outer backward therefore cannot apply loss weights, accumulation scaling, or Matryoshka dimension weights to those parameters. For example, multiplying the returned loss by zero leaves a nonzero head gradient on current main (`688fd663`). Default cosine/dot scoring has no trainable head and is unaffected.

This was found through source analysis and reproduced with synthetic data, a locally initialized BERT, and real SentenceTransformerTrainer optimizer steps; it is not a claim of personal production use.

The change defers score backward only when registered trainable parameters exist outside the encoder module. It replays score RNG, autocast and registered buffer state, applies the incoming gradient to each score chunk, then replays already-scaled embedding gradients. Matryoshka passes dimension weights into the same calculation. Parameter-free/frozen/buffer-only heads retain the existing score/backward path without input clones or state snapshots. Existing calculate_loss overrides without the new keyword keep their original contract (and its trainable-head limitation).

Minimal reproduction on unchanged main:
```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer import losses

class Encoder(nn.Linear):
    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self
    def forward(self, features):
        return {"sentence_embedding": super().forward(features["values"])}

class Head(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(1.3))
    def forward(self, a, b):
        return (a @ b.T) * self.scale

torch.manual_seed(123)
head = Head()
loss = losses.CachedMultipleNegativesRankingLoss(
    Encoder(5, 4), similarity_fct=head, scale=1, mini_batch_size=2
)
features = [{"values": torch.randn(5, 5)} for _ in range(2)]
value = loss(features, None)
print(head.scale.grad)  # expected None; main already has a gradient
(value * 0).backward()
print(head.scale.grad)  # expected zero; main retains the head gradient
```

Validation: Python 3.12.14, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, Transformers 5.23.0, Accelerate 1.15.0.
```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest \
  tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_gradcache_heads.py \
  tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_gradcache.py \
  tests/sparse_encoder/losses/test_cached_splade.py \
  tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_matryoshka.py -q
# 192 passed
```

Coverage includes real Trainer accumulation, CPU bf16, zero/negative outer and dimension weights, repeated backward, unused/frozen grad=None, shared encoder/head parameters, parameter/buffer aliases, input mutation and cache collection. The first head regression fails on clean main. Six additional isolated actual-engine checks pass on Torch 2.2.2; this is not full-package minimum-version validation. Ruff 0.15.6 lint/format and git diff --check pass. Independent byte-address enumeration accepted 5,429 of 20,000 mixed-dtype view pairs without collisions.

Limitations: two-process CPU Gloo fails during socket initialization with Operation not permitted, before gradient assertions. No security settings were changed. DDP head synchronization (including Trainer wrapping), CUDA/GradScaler, MPS, FSDP, DeepSpeed and compile remain unverified. This change does not add head all-reduce. Deferred input isolation conservatively rejects unproven overlapping layouts; arbitrary mutable non-Tensor state and custom embed_minibatch implementations are not covered. Trainable non-Parameter buffers are rejected explicitly. Distinct registered tensors sharing storage with a buffer are rejected before encoding, including disjoint buffer views; repeated references to the same Tensor are supported. Head recomputation adds work; noisy CPU smoke timings do not establish a speedup or a deployment overhead estimate.

Existing shared encoding (#3761), the merged GradCache engine (#3862), and loss-head checkpointing (#4272) are separate work; this adds neither shared encoding nor checkpoint support. Bounded all-state PR/issue searches found no competing head-scaling fix.

AI disclosure: Codex continued an AI-assisted prototype, implemented and reviewed these changes, wrote/ran the regressions and prepared this description. An independent reviewer reproduced and verified the buffer-storage alias guard. Kept as draft because distributed and accelerator validation remain outstanding.

title: fix(model): quantize token embeddings and dict outputs in encode()
body:
## Summary

`SentenceTransformer.encode()` applied `precision` quantization to whatever `_inference` returned, so it only worked for the default `output_value="sentence_embedding"` mode. With `output_value="token_embeddings"` the quantized matrices silently came back as `ndarray`s instead of tensors, and with `output_value=None` it crashed with a raw `TypeError` (`'<=' not supported between instances of 'dict' and 'dict'`) from `quantize_embeddings` on the list of dicts.

This adds a mode-aware quantization step: token embeddings are quantized per matrix with shared batch calibration, and for `output_value=None` the `sentence_embedding` (stacked, shared ranges) and `token_embeddings` entries of each dict are quantized, converting the results back to tensors so the unquantized return types are preserved. Non-embedding dict entries (e.g. `attention_mask`) are left untouched. Fixes #2882.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `sentence_transformers/sentence_transformer/model.py` | `encode()` now quantizes via new `_quantize_encode_output()` helper (mode-aware; `output_value="token_embeddings"` and `None` handled, `sentence_embedding` unchanged); `precision` docstring updated |
| `tests/sentence_transformer/test_model.py` | 8 new regression tests: `test_encode_quantization_token_embeddings` and `test_encode_quantization_output_value_none` across int8/uint8/binary/ubinary |

## Verification

All commands run offline against the tiny test model (`sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors`) with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and proxy env vars unset (sandbox `httpx` quirk):

- Issue repro (pre-fix): `output_value=None, precision="int8"` raised `TypeError`; `output_value="token_embeddings", precision="int8"` returned `ndarray`s. Post-fix: `None` mode returns a list of dicts, token mode returns a list of `torch.Tensor`s.
- New tests: `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/test_model.py::test_encode_quantization_token_embeddings tests/sentence_transformer/test_model.py::test_encode_quantization_output_value_none` — **8 passed**.
- Negative control: with the fix stashed, all 8 new tests fail on the pristine tree.
- Existing suites: `test_encode_quantization` + `test_encode_truncate` + `test_prompt_output_value_None` + `tests/util/test_quantization.py` — **91 passed, 51 skipped** (skips are CUDA-gated). Re-ran on a cherry-pick of this branch onto upstream `main` (688fd66): **36 passed** (8 new + 28 existing quantization tests).
- `ruff check` clean; `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

Note: a singular input with `precision="int8"/"uint8"` still raises the documented `quantize_embeddings` `ValueError` (ranges cannot be calibrated from a single embedding) — unchanged, consistent with the sentence-embedding mode.

title: Prevent autocast overflow in GOR moment accumulation
body:
## Problem

Under fp16 autocast, GlobalOrthogonalRegularizationLoss sums a half-precision similarity matrix before dividing. A batch of 512 highly similar embeddings produces infinite losses and nonfinite gradients, although the expected moments are bounded.

Reproducer on main 688fd663, CPU PyTorch 2.7.1:
```python
import torch
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.losses import GlobalOrthogonalRegularizationLoss
loss = GlobalOrthogonalRegularizationLoss(torch.nn.Identity())
x = torch.ones(512, 64, requires_grad=True)
with torch.autocast("cpu", dtype=torch.float16):
    parts = loss.compute_loss_from_embeddings([x])
sum(parts.values()).backward()
print(parts, torch.isfinite(x.grad).all())
```
Before: both parts inf, gradients nonfinite. Expected and after: gor_mean=1, gor_second_moment=0.984375, finite gradients. Found through code analysis and reproduced locally, not in a deployed user model.

## Change

Accumulate fp16/bf16 similarity moments in float32. Float32/float64 paths remain unchanged. This does not introduce the feature-Gram optimization from the earlier performance proposal #4115 (already closed). The temporary similarity buffer uses twice the storage under half-precision autocast; no memory or performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu, Transformers 5.23.0:
- Focused GOR module: 14 passed. Unchanged implementation: both fp16 regressions fail; other 12 pass.
- GOR plus similarity utility tests: 168 passed, 6 skipped, 1 deselected. The deselected sparse-model fixture needs a pretrained Hub model; setup first errored because socksio was unavailable.
- Three actual Linear+SGD steps under fp16 CPU autocast: finite parameter gradients and loss 1.94414 -> 1.94199 -> 1.93948.
- Independent automated checks preserve float64 output, pass gradcheck, and retain zero singleton losses/gradients under fp16/bf16 autocast.
- Full repository pre-commit --all-files passes (pinned Ruff check/format and typos); git diff --check passes.
- Additional compatibility run: PyTorch 2.2.0+cpu, Transformers 5.0.0, NumPy 1.26.4, Python 3.12.14: focused 14 passed; GOR plus similarity utilities 165 passed, 7 skipped, 1 deselected, 2 expected failures. This is not the complete minimum-dependency CI matrix.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_global_orthogonal_regularization.py tests/util/test_similarity.py -k 'not test_pairwise_angle_sim_even_and_odd_sparse_embeddings' -q --override-ini='addopts='
```

CUDA and the complete repository/dependency matrix were not run. Quality, Unit tests and Minimum version tests workflows await maintainer approval; no remote CI pass is claimed.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description. The contribution and its follow-up are author-directed; no human or maintainer approval is claimed.

title: Add semantic_search_mlxvs: semantic search on the GPU of Apple silicon Macs
body:
Closes #4370

Adds `semantic_search_mlxvs` to `sentence_transformers.util.quantization`. It is semantic search on the GPU of Apple silicon Macs through [mlxvs](https://github.com/mikepapadim/mlxvs), and mirrors `semantic_search_faiss` and `semantic_search_usearch`.

### What it does

- **Signature and results:** the same as the faiss and usearch helpers: `query_embeddings`, `corpus_embeddings` / `corpus_index`, `corpus_precision`, `top_k`, `ranges`, `calibration_embeddings`, `rescore`, `rescore_multiplier`, `exact`, `output_index`. Results come back as `[[{"corpus_id", "score"}, ...], ...]`, with the search time.
- **Precisions:** `float32`, `int8`, `uint8`, `ubinary` and `binary`.
- **Rescoring:** quantized corpora are rescored with the float queries as the faiss helper does, dequantizing int8 / uint8 with `ranges` / `calibration_embeddings`.
- **Exact search (default):** float and integer corpora are scored by inner product on the GPU; binary corpora by Hamming distance with popcounts. Without rescoring, binary scores are Hamming distances, as faiss reports them.
- **Approximate search (`exact=False`):** a CAGRA graph index (NVIDIA cuVS's graph search), or an IVF index of the bits for binary corpora. Corpora of 1,000 rows or fewer are searched exactly.
- **Index reuse:** `output_index=True` returns the index (the corpus on the GPU, an `mlxvs.CagraIndex` or an `mlxvs.IvfBinaryIndex`), which `corpus_index=` takes on later calls.

### Also in the PR

- **Docs:** `docs/package_reference/util/quantization.md` lists the function.
- **Example:** `examples/.../embedding-quantization/semantic_search_mlxvs.py`, the usearch example adapted, linked from that folder's README.
- **Dependencies:** the test and dev dependency lists get `mlxvs>=0.15.2; sys_platform == 'darwin' and platform_machine == 'arm64'`, so nothing changes on Linux or Windows.

### Tests

Added to `tests/util/test_quantization.py`, with a `skip_without_mlxvs` mark like the faiss and usearch ones. The parametrized rescoring and calibration tests now also cover `semantic_search_mlxvs`, for int8 and uint8. The new tests check:

- unsupported precisions are rejected
- inner-product ranking, exact and approximate
- results match exact search on a larger corpus, and the returned index can be reused
- binary and ubinary give the same results
- Hamming distances are exact
- short and empty corpora
- rescoring of embeddings whose dimension isn't a multiple of 8
- top_k above 256
- approximate binary search with rescoring

On an M3 Pro, all 171 tests of the file outside the faiss ones pass. The faiss tests crash in my local environment from the known OpenMP clash between faiss-cpu and torch on macOS, with or without this change. Linux and Windows CI skips the mlxvs tests.

### Numbers

OpenAI ada-002 embeddings (982,790 × 1536), 1,000 queries, top 10, on a MacBook Pro M3 Pro. `rescore_multiplier=4`.

| | search | recall@10 | index |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `util.semantic_search` (torch, MPS) float32 | 3,206 ms | 1.000 | |
| `semantic_search_mlxvs` float32 exact | 877 ms | 1.000 | 1 s |
| `semantic_search_mlxvs` float32 approximate | 159 ms | 0.977 | 103 s |
| `semantic_search_usearch` float32 approximate | 150 ms | 0.971 | 334 s |
| `semantic_search_mlxvs` int8 exact + rescore | 1,135 ms | 0.957 | 0 s |
| `semantic_search_usearch` int8 exact + rescore | 14,871 ms | 0.957 | 102 s |
| `semantic_search_mlxvs` ubinary exact + rescore | 893 ms | 0.744 | 0 s |
| `semantic_search_usearch` ubinary exact + rescore | 3,140 ms | 0.744 | 27 s |

### Usage

```python
from sentence_transformers.util.quantization import quantize_embeddings, semantic_search_mlxvs

corpus = quantize_embeddings(corpus_embeddings, precision="ubinary")
results, search_time, index = semantic_search_mlxvs(
    query_embeddings, corpus_embeddings=corpus, corpus_precision="ubinary", top_k=10, output_index=True
)
```

Install: `pip install mlxvs` (macOS 14+, Apple silicon).

title: [fix] Accept pathlib.Path as model_name_or_path in the other model classes
body:
#4326 made `SentenceTransformer` convert a `pathlib.Path` `model_name_or_path` to `str`. Its description says the other three model classes already accept a `Path`. That holds only when the path exists. When a `Path` is not a local directory, `CrossEncoder`, `SparseEncoder` and `MultiVectorEncoder` raise a confusing error instead of the `FileNotFoundError` that `SentenceTransformer` raises for the same input.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder, MultiVectorEncoder, SentenceTransformer, SparseEncoder

for cls in (SentenceTransformer, CrossEncoder, SparseEncoder, MultiVectorEncoder):
    try:
        cls(Path("checkpoints") / "run-1" / "does-not-exist")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{cls.__name__}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

On `main` (7969acfe), on Windows:

```
SentenceTransformer: FileNotFoundError: Path checkpoints\run-1\does-not-exist not found
CrossEncoder: TypeError: argument of type 'WindowsPath' is not iterable
SparseEncoder: TypeError: argument of type 'WindowsPath' is not iterable
MultiVectorEncoder: TypeError: argument of type 'WindowsPath' is not iterable
```

On Linux/macOS the other three raise `AttributeError: 'PosixPath' object has no attribute 'count'` from the same line. With this PR, all four raise `FileNotFoundError` on both platforms (three path parts, so the Hub-id check rejects it on POSIX too).

### Cause

When `model_name_or_path` is not a local directory, `BaseModel.__init__` treats it as a Hub id and runs string checks on it: `"\\" in model_name_or_path` and `model_name_or_path.count("/")` (`sentence_transformers/base/model.py`, line 266). `Path` supports neither. On POSIX the first condition short-circuits and `.count()` is the one that fails. Existing directories skip this branch, which is why loading a saved model from a `Path` already works.

### Fix

Same change #4326 made to `SentenceTransformer`: each `__init__` converts a `Path` to `str` before calling `BaseModel.__init__`, and the type hints and docstrings now say `str or Path`. I kept it per class, as #4326 did, so all four follow one pattern.

### Tests

I added `test_missing_pathlib_path_raises_file_not_found` to `tests/base/test_model.py`, parametrized over all four classes. With the source change reverted it gives 3 failed (CrossEncoder, SparseEncoder, MultiVectorEncoder at `base/model.py:266`) and 1 passed (SentenceTransformer); with the fix all four pass. The five affected `test_model.py` files give 1425 passed, 89 skipped, and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (0.15.6, the pre-commit version) are clean on the changed files.

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.11.18, torch 2.15.0+cpu, transformers 5.22.2. I found this by reading the code after #4326, not in a real workflow. I verified the POSIX side of the line-266 check in WSL Ubuntu 24.04, but did not run the test suite on Linux or macOS.

title: Support losses that return a dictionary in MatryoshkaLoss and AdaptiveLayerLoss
body:
## Reference Issues

None that I could find. I found this while testing loss wrappers with custom losses, following the `GlobalOrthogonalRegularizationLoss` documentation example. This was identified through testing and code analysis, not in a real training run.

## What does this implement/fix?

The trainer supports losses that return a dictionary of named components, which `BaseTrainer.track_loss_components` logs individually. However, wrapping such a loss in `MatryoshkaLoss`, `AdaptiveLayerLoss` or `Matryoshka2dLoss` raises a `TypeError`, because the wrappers perform arithmetic on the returned value as if it were a single tensor:

```python
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'int' and 'dict'
```

`AdaptiveLayerLoss` fails similarly, when multiplying the dictionary by the layer weight. This was reproduced on both sentence-transformers 6.2.0 and the main branch.

<details>
<summary>Minimal reproducer</summary>

```python
from torch import nn
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer, losses

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors")

class InfoNCEWithGOR(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, model):
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.info_nce = losses.MultipleNegativesRankingLoss(model)
        self.gor = losses.GlobalOrthogonalRegularizationLoss(model)

    def forward(self, sentence_features, labels=None):
        embeddings = [self.model(f)["sentence_embedding"] for f in sentence_features]
        return {
            "info_nce": self.info_nce.compute_loss_from_embeddings(embeddings, labels),
            **self.gor.compute_loss_from_embeddings(embeddings, labels),
        }

loss = losses.MatryoshkaLoss(model, InfoNCEWithGOR(model), [128, 64])
loss([model.tokenize(["a", "b"]), model.tokenize(["c", "d"])], None)
```

</details>

This matters for anyone combining Matryoshka or adaptive-layer training with a multi-term loss (for example InfoNCE plus a regulariser) who wants to see each term in the training logs.

This PR weights and accumulates each dictionary component separately and returns a dictionary, allowing the trainer to continue logging them individually.

In `AdaptiveLayerLoss`, the KL-divergence term is exposed as a separate `kl_div_loss` component when the underlying loss returns a dictionary. Losses returning a single tensor retain their existing behaviour. The gradient-cache path of `MatryoshkaLoss` is also untouched.

The implementation is consistent with how `SpladeLoss` and `CSRLoss` already handle dictionary-returning losses.

## Any other comments?

Added two regression tests:
- `test_matryoshka_loss_with_dictionary_of_losses`
- `test_adaptive_layer_loss_with_dictionary_of_losses`

Both compare the individual dictionary components against the corresponding existing tensor-based results.

**Testing:**
- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses`: 474 passed, 52 skipped.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files: passed.
- Ran 4 steps of `SentenceTransformerTrainer` with `MatryoshkaLoss` and a custom InfoNCE + GOR loss. `info_nce`, `gor_mean` and `gor_second_moment` were logged separately.

These checks were first run against the original base commit (`a89a0fb`). After rebasing onto the current main (`7969acfe`), I re-ran the full test suite and `make check` in CI on my fork (Ubuntu, Python 3.12, same setup as `tests.yml`): 5595 passed, 432 skipped, and `make check` passed ([run](https://github.com/rishi02102017/sentence-transformers/actions/runs/43306191734)).

PR #4354 also modifies `MatryoshkaLoss`, but in a different section, with no overlapping changes.

**AI assistance:** AI tools helped with investigating the issue, writing the implementation and regression tests, and interpreting test results. I reviewed the changes and test results and am responsible for the final implementation and this contribution.

title: Disable tokenizer truncation in StaticEmbedding
body:
Closes #4366

StaticEmbedding embeds every token (its max_seq_length is inf) and already calls no_padding() on its tokenizer, but it kept any truncation the tokenizer was loaded with. Tokenizers of e.g. sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 truncate to 128 tokens via their tokenizer.json, so a StaticEmbedding built from them silently averaged only the first 128 tokens of each text. See the issue for a reproducer: two different texts that share their first 128 tokens get a similarity of 1.0000 on main and 0.5973 with this change.

Change: call self.tokenizer.no_truncation() next to the existing self.tokenizer.no_padding() in StaticEmbedding.__init__. This covers both a tokenizers.Tokenizer and a PreTrainedTokenizerFast (whose backend is already copied since #4253), and both new modules and loading, since load goes through __init__.

Backwards compatibility: models whose saved tokenizer.json has no truncation, which includes the published static models I checked (static-retrieval-mrl-en-v1, static-similarity-mrl-multilingual-v1, minishlab/potion-base-8M), produce the same outputs. A StaticEmbedding that was saved with a truncating tokenizer now embeds all tokens of texts longer than that limit, which is the behavior max_seq_length == inf describes.

Tests: new test_tokenize_ignores_tokenizer_truncation in tests/sentence_transformer/modules/test_static_embedding.py, parametrized over a tokenizers.Tokenizer and a PreTrainedTokenizerFast with truncation enabled. Both cases fail on main and pass with this change.

```

  103 passed, 4 skipped
python -m pytest tests/sentence_transformer/test_model.py tests/base/modules/test_dense.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_merged_forward.py tests/base/test_model.py -q -k "static or Static"
```

title: [feat] Add Intel XPU support to `start_multi_process_pool`
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds Intel XPU support to `start_multi_process_pool()`.

**Context:** `get_device_name()` already returns `"xpu"`, but the pool only builds a device list for `("cuda", "npu", "neuron")`. On XPU it fell back to 4 CPU workers and left the XPUs idle.

**Change:** add `"xpu"` to that tuple, so when `target_devices` isn't given, the pool uses `xpu:0 … xpu:N-1` from `torch.xpu.device_count()`. Other devices are unaffected.

**Motivation:** I tried to run multi-process encoding on XPUs through the downstream LangChain integration `HuggingFaceEmbeddings(multi_process=True)`, which calls Sentence Transformers' `start_multi_process_pool()` with no arguments, but the pool only started 4 CPU workers.

## How I Verified

Ran this script on a 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 machine (torch 2.15.0+xpu):

```python
import logging
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(format="%(name)s: %(message)s")
    logging.getLogger("sentence_transformers").setLevel(logging.INFO)
    model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
    pool = model.start_multi_process_pool()
    try:
        print(model.encode(["hello", "world"] * 8, pool=pool).shape)
    finally:
        model.stop_multi_process_pool(pool)
```

Results:

| | sentence_transformers.base.model: Starting multi-process pool on devices: |
|---|---|
| Before (`main`) | `cpu, cpu, cpu, cpu` |
| After (this PR) | `xpu:0, xpu:1` |

Existing multi-process tests still pass:

```bash
pytest -q tests/base/test_multi_process.py tests/sentence_transformer/test_multi_process.py
# ................................. [100%]

```

title: [`fix`] Score `main_score_function` in IR evaluators when `score_functions` is unset
body:
Hello!

`InformationRetrievalEvaluator(..., main_score_function="dot")` on a cosine model only scores `cosine`, but still sets `primary_metric` to `dot_ndcg@10`, so `results[evaluator.primary_metric]` raises a `KeyError`. This is the IR counterpart of #4088 for `TripletEvaluator`.

## Failing example

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.evaluation import InformationRetrievalEvaluator

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors")  # similarity_fn_name="cosine"
evaluator = InformationRetrievalEvaluator(
    queries={"q0": "What is the capital of France?"},
    corpus={"d0": "Paris is the capital of France.", "d1": "Berlin is the capital of Germany."},
    relevant_docs={"q0": {"d0"}},
    name="dev",
    main_score_function="dot",
)
results = evaluator(model)
print(evaluator.primary_metric, results[evaluator.primary_metric])
```

On `main`:

```
KeyError: 'dev_dot_ndcg@10'
```

`results` only contains `dev_cosine_*` keys. The same happens with `NanoBEIREvaluator(main_score_function="dot")` (`KeyError: 'NanoBEIR_mean_dot_ndcg@10'`), the sparse IR and NanoBEIR evaluators, and `MultiVectorInformationRetrievalEvaluator(main_score_function="meanmaxsim")` on a `maxsim` model. The legacy `SentenceTransformer.fit` path hits it as well, since it reads `score[evaluator.primary_metric]` after each evaluation.

## Root cause

Since #3976, an evaluator without explicit `score_functions` resolves its scoring per call through `_model_score_functions(model)`, which always returns `{model.similarity_fn_name: model.similarity}`. `main_score_function` is never consulted there, but it is used to name `primary_metric`, so the two disagree whenever the main score function is not the model's own similarity.

## Fix

`_model_score_functions` returns `main_score_function` when it is set, the same fallback `TripletEvaluator` got in #4088. Because `NanoBEIREvaluator` reads its aggregate labels from `self.evaluators[0]._model_score_functions(model)`, the aggregate names follow automatically. The multi-vector override resolves the same name and keeps binding `chunk_elements` onto the scorer. Explicit `score_functions` are untouched, and a `main_score_function` that matches the model's similarity scores exactly as before.

I found this through code analysis, not a production incident.

## Tests

Three regression tests, each failing on `main` and passing with the fix:

- `test_information_retrieval_evaluator.py::test_main_score_function_is_evaluated`
- `test_nanobeir_evaluator.py::test_nanobeir_evaluator_main_score_function_is_evaluated`
- `multi_vector_encoder/evaluation/test_information_retrieval.py::test_ir_evaluator_scores_the_main_score_function`

```
pytest tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation/test_information_retrieval_evaluator.py::test_main_score_function_is_evaluated \
       tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation/test_nanobeir_evaluator.py::test_nanobeir_evaluator_main_score_function_is_evaluated \
       tests/multi_vector_encoder/evaluation/test_information_retrieval.py::test_ir_evaluator_scores_the_main_score_function -q
```

With the source change reverted: `3 failed` (`assert ['cosine'] == ['dot']`, `KeyError: 'NanoBEIR_mean_dot_ndcg@10'`, `assert ['maxsim'] == ['meanmaxsim']`). With the fix: `3 passed`.

```
pytest tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation tests/multi_vector_encoder/evaluation tests/sparse_encoder/evaluation -q
```

`170 passed, 5 skipped`. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.15.6, as pinned in pre-commit) pass on the changed files.

AI assistance: the bug was found through code analysis with an AI coding assistant, and the fix and tests were drafted with it. I reviewed the change and verified it by running the tests above, before and after the fix.

title: Reject concurrent inference calls sharing a process pool
body:
Refs #2955.

Concurrent inference calls sharing a process pool use call-local chunk IDs on the same queues. Either caller can consume the other call's chunks, changing the text-to-embedding mapping or leaving missing chunks that fail during concatenation. This also occurs when separate model objects share the pool.

Reject overlapping calls before submitting any chunks, tracking the input queue in the shared BaseModel dispatcher. Pool dictionary aliases are covered. Sequential reuse, reuse after a reported worker failure, and independent pools remain available. Document the single-caller requirement on start_multi_process_pool().

The public encode() regressions cover same/different models, pool aliases, independent pools and subsequent reuse. Against original product code, the six deterministic cases give **4 failed, 2 passed**. A real CPU worker regression also fails on the original code with a missing chunk during concatenation. With the fix, that regression preserves the active call's embeddings and subsequent sequential results exactly. The existing shared-dispatcher tests cover all four encoder classes and worker-error cleanup.

Validated on macOS 26.6 arm64, Python 3.13.15, PyTorch 2.15.0, Transformers 5.22.1 and Sentence Transformers 6.3.0.dev0, at `ea1d489`:

- `pytest tests/base/test_multi_process.py tests/sentence_transformer/test_multi_process.py -q`: **39 passed, 41 deselected** (the repository's default slow/custom exclusions).
- `pytest 'tests/sentence_transformer/test_multi_process.py::test_multi_process_encode_same_as_standard_encode[cpu]' tests/sentence_transformer/test_multi_process.py::test_concurrent_encode_preserves_real_pool_results -m slow -q`: **2 passed**. The latter is a deterministic reproducer using event-controlled result collection and the tiny BERT fixture.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: Ruff check, Ruff format and typos passed.

Tests used the native virtual environment with the cached tiny BERT fixture in offline mode; commands above omit cache-location arguments. The full project, GPU and other platform matrices were not run locally.

I'm happy to rename anything or follow conventions you prefer.
2. If it does, I'm happy to go whichever way is easier for you to review:
   - **A.** Add the sparse, multi-vector and reranker (CrossEncoder) versions to this PR.
   - **B.** Merge this PR, then add those versions in follow-up PRs.

   Either way, their NanoBEIR evaluators would become thin subclasses, as `NanoBEIREvaluator` does here. For the reranker, the subset that provides the candidates to rerank would be configurable, with `bm25` as the default, as it is today.
3. If it fits the project's direction, I'd also like to look into image collections such as NanoViDoRe later.

## Usage

A Nano collection is a dataset with three subsets, `corpus`, `queries` and `qrels`, laid out like [NanoBEIR-en](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sentence-transformers/NanoBEIR-en). Each split is one retrieval task. In NanoBEIR-en, for example, the splits are `NanoMSMARCO`, `NanoSciFact` and so on.

### 1. NanoBEIR, as before

Existing code keeps working without changes:

```python
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.evaluation import NanoBEIREvaluator

evaluator = NanoBEIREvaluator(dataset_names=["msmarco", "scifact"])
results = evaluator(model)
evaluator.primary_metric  # "NanoBEIR_mean_cosine_ndcg@10", as before
```

### 2. Any Nano collection, with `NanoRetrievalEvaluator`

Instead of short names, `NanoRetrievalEvaluator` takes the ID of a dataset on the Hub. It evaluates every split by default, or only the ones given in `splits`:

```python
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.evaluation import NanoRetrievalEvaluator

evaluator = NanoRetrievalEvaluator("hakari-bench/NanoCoIR")
results = evaluator(model)
evaluator.primary_metric  # "NanoCoIR_mean_cosine_ndcg@10"

evaluator = NanoRetrievalEvaluator("hakari-bench/NanoMLDR", splits=["en", "ja"])
results = evaluator(model)  # "NanoMLDR_en_...", "NanoMLDR_ja_..." and "NanoMLDR_mean_..."
```

### 3. Several collections at once

This needs no new class. The existing `SequentialEvaluator` runs the evaluators one after another, and with `main_score_function=np.mean` its main score is the mean of their primary metrics:

```python
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers.base.evaluation import SequentialEvaluator

evaluator = SequentialEvaluator(
    [NanoBEIREvaluator(), NanoRetrievalEvaluator("hakari-bench/NanoCoIR")],
    main_score_function=np.mean,
)
results = evaluator(model)
results["NanoBEIR_mean_cosine_ndcg@10"]  # NanoBEIR, as today
results["NanoCoIR_mean_cosine_ndcg@10"]  # NanoCoIR
results["sequential_score"]              # the mean of the two
```

This also works during training. With `metric_for_best_model="eval_sequential_score"` and `load_best_model_at_end=True`, the Trainer keeps the checkpoint with the best mean score.

However, this approach has two shortcomings:

- The mean is always named `sequential_score`, so the name doesn't say which metric is averaged.
- The mean isn't written to the model card. Only the results of each collection are.

Both could be fixed with a small change to `SequentialEvaluator`, or with a small subclass of it, that reports a named overall score such as `my_suite_mean_cosine_ndcg@10` and stores it in the model card. In the issue, you mentioned something like a `BenchmarkEvaluator` for running a suite of datasets at once, and this may be where it fits. Personally, I think a small change to `SequentialEvaluator` would be the better option.

## Changes

- **`NanoRetrievalEvaluator(dataset_id, splits=None, name=None, ...)`**
  - The other arguments are the same as in `NanoBEIREvaluator`.
  - By default, it evaluates every split. Its name is taken from the last part of `dataset_id`, so it is `NanoCoIR` in the example above.
  - Metrics are named `{name}_{split}_...` for each task and `{name}_mean_...` for the aggregate.
- **`NanoBEIREvaluator`**
  - It is now a subclass of `NanoRetrievalEvaluator`. What remains in it is NanoBEIR specific: it validates its short dataset names (`"msmarco"`), maps them to split names (`"NanoMSMARCO"`), keeps its existing metric names (`NanoMSMARCO_...`) and keeps its own `get_config_dict()`.
  - `SparseNanoBEIREvaluator` and `MultiVectorNanoBEIREvaluator` subclass it, so they pick up the change without being modified.
- **Model card:** `NanoRetrievalEvaluator` is recognized as an information retrieval evaluator.
- **Docs:** the docstrings explain two things:
  - How to combine several collections with `SequentialEvaluator` (see "Several collections at once" above).
  - How to load translated NanoBEIR collections, for example `NanoRetrievalEvaluator("lightonai/NanoBEIR-de")`, so that their metrics get their own prefix.

## Tests

- The new `tests/sentence_transformer/evaluation/test_nano_retrieval_evaluator.py` uses a small in-memory collection, so it doesn't need network access. It also checks that a split named like the aggregate (e.g. `mean`) raises an error, instead of its metrics being silently overwritten.
- Compatibility: I ran `NanoBEIREvaluator`, `SparseNanoBEIREvaluator` and `MultiVectorNanoBEIREvaluator` on the real NanoBEIR datasets in 8 configurations, on both `main` and this branch. The results, primary metric, names, CSV files, config and model card metrics are identical.
- The `SequentialEvaluator` pattern, with `static-retrieval-mrl-en-v1`: with NanoBEIR-en, NanoCoIR and NanoMLDR, `sequential_score` is the mean of the three primary metrics, and none of the metric keys collide. Combining `NanoBEIREvaluator()` with `NanoRetrievalEvaluator("lightonai/NanoBEIR-de")` causes no collisions either.

Commands I ran:

```bash
make check
make docs
pytest tests/{sentence_transformer,sparse_encoder,multi_vector_encoder,cross_encoder}/evaluation tests/*/test_model_card*.py
```

All pass: 376 passed and 11 skipped on Python 3.12. The tests also pass on Python 3.10 with the minimum dependency versions, as in the `min-versions` workflow.

## AI assistance

I used Claude Code to help write the implementation, the tests and this description. I reviewed every change and verified the results above myself.

Thanks for taking the time to review this. Any feedback is welcome.

title: [fix] Use the untruncated embedding dimension in MatryoshkaLoss and EmbedDistillLoss
body:
Fixes #4353

`truncate_dim` only applies in `encode()`, but `MatryoshkaLoss` and `EmbedDistillLoss` used `get_embedding_dimension()` (the truncated size) as the size of the forward-pass embeddings. With `truncate_dim` set on the student, `MatryoshkaLoss(MSELoss)` never truncated the full-size teacher labels and crashed on a shape mismatch, and `EmbedDistillLoss` built its projection for the wrong input size. I found it by code analysis, not in use.

```python
import torch
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer import losses

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors", truncate_dim=64)
features = [model.preprocess(["A man is eating.", "A woman is reading."])]
losses.MatryoshkaLoss(model, losses.MSELoss(model), [128, 64])(features, torch.randn(2, 128))
losses.EmbedDistillLoss(model, projection_dim=32)(features, torch.randn(2, 32))
```

- `main`: `RuntimeError` in both (`size of tensor a (64) must match ... (128)` and `addmm: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (2x128 and 64x32)`).
- With this PR: both return a finite loss.

Realistic case: Matryoshka or projection distillation with a student that was saved or loaded with `truncate_dim` (often set for evaluation), trained against precomputed full-size teacher embeddings. It crashes at the first training step.

**Change:**
- `MatryoshkaLoss.forward` and `EmbedDistillLoss` (`__init__`, `load_projection`) use `_get_untruncated_embedding_dimension()`, which `MatryoshkaLoss.__init__` already uses.
- `EmbedDistillLoss` falls back to `get_embedding_dimension()` for models without that method. That covers `SparseMSELoss`, which inherits `load_projection`: `SparseEncoder` has no `truncate_dim`, so its dimension is already untruncated.
- `BaseTrainer.override_model_in_loss` also binds `_get_untruncated_embedding_dimension` onto DDP/compile wrappers, next to `get_embedding_dimension`, so the Matryoshka path keeps working under DDP.

**Tests:**
- `test_mse_loss_matryoshka_with_model_truncate_dim` in `tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_matryoshka.py`, for a bare model and one wrapped through `override_model_in_loss`.
- `test_projection_with_model_truncate_dim` in `tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_embed_distill.py`, for `EmbedDistillLoss` and `MSELoss(projection_dim=...)`, including a `save_projection`/`load_projection` round trip.
- `test_sparse_mse_load_projection` in `tests/sparse_encoder/losses/test_sparse_mse.py` guards the `SparseMSELoss` path.
- The four `truncate_dim` tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.

- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_matryoshka.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_embed_distill.py tests/sparse_encoder/losses/test_sparse_mse.py`: 69 passed
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff check, ruff format, typos pass

**AI disclosure:** I used Claude Code (Anthropic) to trace the dimension handling in these losses, write the reproducer, and draft the tests and this description. I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: [`fix`] Run the EmbedDistillLoss and MSELoss projection in float32 for low-precision models
body:
`EmbedDistillLoss` and its `MSELoss` subclass crash on the first forward pass as soon as `projection_dim` is set and the student model runs in anything other than float32. The projection is an `nn.Linear` created in float32, while a model loaded with `model_kwargs={"torch_dtype": torch.bfloat16}` (or converted with `model.to(dtype=...)`) produces bfloat16 / float16 / float64 embeddings:

```python
import torch
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from sentence_transformers.sentence_transformer.losses import MSELoss

model = SentenceTransformer(
    "sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors",
    model_kwargs={"torch_dtype": torch.bfloat16},
)
loss = MSELoss(model, projection_dim=1024)  # teacher dim
features = [model.preprocess(["a", "b"])]
labels = torch.randn(2, 1024)
loss(features, labels)
# main:    RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype, but got BFloat16 and Float
# this PR: tensor(..., grad_fn=<MeanBackward0>)
```

Training such a model with the `SentenceTransformerTrainer` fails the same way, because `prepare_loss` moves the loss to the model's device but not to its dtype. Without `projection_dim` the loss is unaffected, since the teacher embeddings are already cast to the student dtype.

**Root cause:** `EmbedDistillLoss.compute_loss_from_embeddings` (`sentence_transformer/losses/embed_distill.py`) applies the float32 projection directly to the student embeddings. It also casts the teacher embeddings to the student dtype *before* the projection, so even with the projection running, `mse` / `l2` would compare a float32 projected student against a lower-precision teacher.

**Fix:** cast the student embeddings to the projection's dtype before projecting, and cast the teacher embeddings to the (projected) student dtype afterwards. The projection and the loss stay in float32, which is what #4193 did for the `SoftmaxLoss` classifier three weeks ago with the same error message. Models without a projection, and float32 models, behave exactly as before.

**Test:** `tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_embed_distill.py::test_projection_model_dtypes` mirrors `test_softmax.py::test_model_dtypes`: a tiny `WordEmbeddings` model in float32 / float16 / bfloat16 / float64, `MSELoss` and `EmbedDistillLoss` with `projection_dim=4`, asserting a finite float32 loss and finite, non-zero gradients on both the projection and the model. On main the six non-float32 cases fail with the `RuntimeError` above; with this change all eight pass.

```
pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_embed_distill.py -k test_projection_model_dtypes
# main:    6 failed, 2 passed
# this PR: 8 passed
pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_embed_distill.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_softmax.py
# this PR: 43 passed
ruff check + ruff format --check (0.15.6) on the two changed files: clean
```

Tested with Python 3.13.15, torch 2.15.0 (CPU), transformers 5.22.2. I found this through code analysis (comparing the losses that own float32 parameters against the #4193 fix), not in actual use.

**AI assistance:** The bug was found through code analysis with an AI coding assistant, and the fix and the regression test were drafted with it. I then verified the fail-before and pass-after runs listed above locally.

title: Speed up dataset column to list conversion throughout ST
body:
With `datasets` 4 and later, `dataset["text"]` returns a lazy `Column`. `mine_hard_negatives` converts the anchor and positive columns, and a `corpus` passed as a column, with `list(column)`. Iterating a `Column` formats one row at a time, which costs about 35 µs per row here, so a 200k-row column takes about 7 s to convert before any mining starts.

This PR adds a small `_to_list` helper that slices a `Column` first (`list(column[:])`), so the whole column is formatted in one batch. All other inputs (lists, tuples, generators, NumPy arrays, and plain lists from `datasets` < 4) still go through `list()` unchanged. On text columns, `list(column[:])` and `list(column)` give the same strings under the default, `python`, `numpy`, `torch`, `pandas`, and `arrow` formats, with `with_transform`, and after `select`, `shuffle`, and `filter`, on `datasets` 4.0.0 and 5.1.0. A randomized comparison of 700 `mine_hard_negatives` calls between `main` and this branch gave identical datasets. The calls covered all four output formats, both sampling strategies, margins and score filters, `include_positives`, formatted datasets, and list, tuple, generator, deque, array, and `Column` corpora.

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| converting a 200k-row text column | 7.31 s | 0.30 s |
| `mine_hard_negatives`, 2k pairs, 50k-row `Column` corpus, embeddings from `cache_folder` | 2.99 s | 1.83 s |
| same, embeddings computed with a static model | 19.8 s | 18.3 s |
| 200 pairs, no corpus | 0.111 s | 0.106 s |

Medians of 5 to 9 alternating rounds in one process, on one CPU thread of a shared Ryzen 5 5600X (Python 3.14, torch 2.15 CPU, datasets 5.1.0). The third row is within noise: the saving is a fixed amount per row, so it matters most with cheap encoders or cached embeddings. I added `test_corpus_input_types`, which runs a list, tuple, generator, and `Column` corpus through `mine_hard_negatives` and fails on `main` for the column case because it checks that the `Column` is not iterated row by row.

AI assistance: Claude Code found this, wrote the change and the test, and ran the benchmarks.

title: Fix TSDAE retokenization for untied decoder vocabularies
body:
Fixes #4345. When an untied TSDAE decoder has a different vocabulary but uses the same tokenizer class, it can receive token IDs from the encoder instead of its own tokenizer. The reconstruction loss then uses the wrong target IDs, even though the loss can remain finite.

For untied decoders, compare the token-to-ID mappings and use the existing retokenization path when they differ. The existing tokenizer-class check remains in place. Tied decoders skip this vocabulary comparison because they receive added encoder tokens later during initialization. Resizing and weight tying remain unchanged.

The four new CPU test cases use tiny BERT checkpoints created locally, so no models need to be downloaded. They cover decoder inputs and cross-entropy target labels, the fast path for equivalent vocabularies, added-token resizing, shared encoder/decoder/LM-head weights, and finite, nonzero gradients during backpropagation.

Validation (Python 3.12.1, torch 2.15.0+cpu):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_denoising_auto_encoder.py -q
# 11 passed with Transformers 5.22.2 / Hub 2.4.0
# 11 passed with Transformers 5.0.0 / Hub 1.3.0 / Datasets 4.4.2

python -m pytest tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_denoising_auto_encoder.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_gist_embed.py tests/sentence_transformer/losses/test_cached_gist_embed.py -q
# 39 passed

pre-commit run --all-files
# Ruff 0.15.6 lint/format and typos 1.45.0 passed

git diff --check
# passed
```

On unchanged main (45925b08), the four new cases give 1 failed / 3 passed. The differing-vocabulary case receives the wrong reconstruction labels. The original issue reproducer now passes the expected IDs to the decoder. A separate native CPU Trainer smoke test completed one step, with finite loss and updated encoder weights.

Related work: #1467 fixes decoding inside retokenization, while #894 concerns added tokens in tied models. This PR fixes when retokenization is triggered for an untied decoder.

Limitations: I did not run the full test suite or validate on GPU, the minimum supported Torch version, other Python versions, or model quality. The fix does not cover tokenizers with the same vocabulary but different settings.

I used codex to help implement the fix and write tests. I found the bug through code analysis.

title: Add `kernels` support for MaxSim, and Ward clustering, and transformers backbones
body:
Hello!

## Pull Request overview

* Add optional Hub kernel support for Transformer backbones across all four model types
* Accelerate MaxSim, MeanMaxSim, and hierarchical token pooling in MultiVectorEncoder
* Use model similarity in multi-vector losses by default and document kernel configuration

## Details

I've added `use_kernels` and `kernel_config` to the model constructors so users can enable optimized implementations without changing their encoding, scoring, or training calls. Backbone kernels use Transformers' existing integration. For multi-vector models, I've also added default providers for MaxSim scoring and Ward clustering:

* https://huggingface.co/kernels/sentence-transformers/late-interaction-kernels
* https://huggingface.co/kernels/sentence-transformers/ward-clustering

Install the optional dependencies with `pip install "sentence-transformers[kernels]"`. For MaxSim acceleration, the following example requires CUDA and Triton:

```python
from sentence_transformers import MultiVectorEncoder

model = MultiVectorEncoder("lightonai/mLateOn", device="cuda", use_kernels=True)

queries = ["What is the capital of France?", "Which planet is known as the Red Planet?"]
documents = ["Paris is the capital of France.", "Mars is known as the Red Planet."]

query_embeddings = model.encode_query(queries)
document_embeddings = model.encode_document(documents)

scores = model.similarity(query_embeddings, document_embeddings)
print(scores)
# tensor([[ 9.6585,  9.3487],
#         [11.2298, 11.5521]], device='cuda:0')
```

`use_kernels=True` selects the default providers. Users can pass a Transformers `KernelConfig` to override individual operations with their own providers, which also enables kernels implicitly. These are runtime settings, so they are not saved in model checkpoints. Kernels remain opt-in, and the existing implementations are used when no compatible replacement is available.

The four multi-vector losses now use `model.similarity` or `model.similarity_pairwise` by default, so kernel settings and MeanMaxSim also carry into training. Passing an explicit `similarity_fct` still lets users choose different training scores. Standalone scoring utilities retain their usual implementations.

**Compatibility note:** Multi-vector losses now default to the model's similarity function, including when kernels are disabled. For models configured with MeanMaxSim, this changes training score scales and can affect existing hyperparameters or teacher labels. Pass the previous ColBERT scoring function explicitly as `similarity_fct` to retain the previous behavior.

I've kept one batched token-pooling path for reference and kernel clustering. Poolers inherit the model's kernel settings unless configured explicitly. The pooling code continues to handle protected tokens, normalization, and straight-through gradients.

For the first 5,000 SciFact titles and abstracts, using `lightonai/mLateOn`, bf16, batch size 32, and an RTX 3090, the Ward benchmark in the documentation gives:

| Operation | Without kernels (fastcluster) | Ward kernel |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pooling existing embeddings | 7.00s | 1.02s |
| Encoding and pooling | 23.14s | 18.91s |

This is about 6.9x faster pooling and an 18% reduction in total encoding and pooling time for that workload.

Validation includes 339 passing tests with 70 skipped on Transformers 5.20.0 and kernels 0.17.2, fresh Hub loads on Windows and Linux, and pooling output and gradient comparisons. The eight rebuilt Ward provider variants each passed 152 tests. Lint, formatting, and typo checks also passed.

- Tom Aarsen

title: [fix] Keep the (0, dim) shape when encoding an empty input
body:
`SentenceTransformer.encode([])` returns a 1-D array of shape `(0,)` (and `torch.Size([0])` with `convert_to_tensor=True`). The `encode` docstring says the default return value is "a 2d numpy array with shape [num_inputs, output_dimension]", so for no inputs it should be `(0, output_dimension)`.

I hit this while running my RAG project, which embeds document chunks in batches with `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` and stacks them. When a batch had no chunks, stacking failed:

```python
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
print(model.encode([]).shape)  # (0,), expected (0, 384)
np.vstack([model.encode(["a"]), model.encode([])])
# ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly,
# but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 384 and the array at index 1 has size 0
```

Versions: sentence-transformers 6.2.0, torch 2.15.0, transformers 5.22.2, numpy 2, Python 3.12, macOS (MPS).

### Cause

For empty input, `encode` replaces the result with `np.array([])` / `torch.tensor([])` (from #2759, which fixed the crash on empty input). That keeps the result empty but drops the embedding dimension.

### Change

When there are no inputs and `output_value="sentence_embedding"`, `encode` now builds a `(0, dim)` float32 array, with `dim` taken from the model's untruncated embedding dimension and the effective `truncate_dim`. It then follows the normal path: `quantize_embeddings` already returns correctly-shaped empty outputs for 2-D input (b1175191), so `int8`/`uint8` give `(0, dim)` and `binary`/`ubinary` give `(0, (dim + 7) // 8)` with the same dtypes as non-empty output. With `convert_to_tensor=True`, the empty tensor stays on the model's device as before.

If the model's embedding dimension is unknown, the previous behavior is kept. `output_value="token_embeddings"` or `None`, and the `convert_to_numpy=False`/`convert_to_tensor=False` list output (`[]`), are unchanged.

### Tests

`test_empty_encode` now also checks that the empty output has the same width and dtype as a non-empty `encode` with the same `precision`, `truncate_dim` and `normalize_embeddings`, for both numpy and tensor output. On `main`, 108 of its 144 cases fail with the new assertions; with this change all 144 pass.

Run locally with this change on `main` @ d936d0bd (macOS, Python 3.12). After rebasing onto aebc76cc (a docs-only commit), `test_empty_encode` was rerun: 144 passed.

- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer -n 6`: 1522 passed, 211 skipped (default markers)
- `pytest -m slow tests/sentence_transformer/test_multi_process.py -k empty`: 12 passed
- `pytest tests/util` (CPU): 1367 passed, 61 skipped, same as `main`
- `pytest tests/base` and `pytest tests/cross_encoder` (CPU): the same results as `main` (identical set of failing tests on both). The failures come from my local environment, mostly the optional `torchcodec` not being installed for the video tests.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files (ruff check, ruff format, typos): pass

Not run: `tests/sparse_encoder` and `tests/multi_vector_encoder`, because `SparseEncoder.encode` and `MultiVectorEncoder.encode` are separate methods that this PR does not change. Also not run on CUDA, Linux or Windows.

title: [fix] Accept tensor and multi-vector calibration in quantize_embeddings
body:
## Problem

`quantize_embeddings` already converts `embeddings` from PyTorch tensors and lists of multi-vector matrices into NumPy arrays. However, `calibration_embeddings` and `ranges` are left unchanged, which causes errors when calibration data is provided as a tensor or as a list of tensors.

For example, using the output of `encode(..., convert_to_tensor=True)` or `MultiVectorEncoder.encode_document()` (which returns a list of `(num_tokens, dim)` tensors by default) can lead to the following errors:

```python
import torch
from sentence_transformers.util import quantize_embeddings

calibration = torch.randn(1000, 16)
documents = torch.randn(10, 16)
quantize_embeddings(documents, "int8", calibration_embeddings=calibration)
# TypeError: min() got an unexpected keyword argument 'axis'

mv_calibration = [torch.randn(n, 16) for n in (40, 35, 50)]
mv_documents = [torch.randn(n, 16) for n in (12, 8)]
quantize_embeddings(mv_documents, "int8", calibration_embeddings=mv_calibration)
# ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence. The requested array has an inhomogeneous shape ...

ranges = torch.stack((calibration.min(dim=0).values, calibration.max(dim=0).values))
quantize_embeddings(documents, "int8", ranges=ranges)
# AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'astype'
```

The same calibration data works correctly when provided as a NumPy array, so the issue is input format handling rather than the quantization logic itself.


## Changes

* Updated `_get_quantization_ranges` to convert `calibration_embeddings` into NumPy arrays through a dedicated `_calibration_to_numpy` helper. Tensors are handled using `_tensor_to_numpy`, which also supports `bfloat16`, while lists of vectors and multi-vector matrices are stacked into a single array.
* Added tensor conversion for `ranges` in `quantize_embeddings`, using `_tensor_to_numpy` for consistency.
* Updated the type hints and docstring to explicitly document the supported input formats.

Existing NumPy inputs retain their previous behavior and follow the same code path as before.

`semantic_search_faiss` and `semantic_search_usearch` also call `_get_quantization_ranges`, so they crashed the same way with a tensor `calibration_embeddings`. With the fix, both return the same results as with the NumPy calibration (checked locally with a uint8 FAISS index and an int8 USearch index).

## Existing work

I checked both open and closed issues and pull requests to make sure this problem wasn't already addressed. The closest related PR is #4025, which focuses on computing shared multi-vector quantization ranges only once. It does not address the supported formats for calibration inputs.

## Validation

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12.10, torch 2.15.0+cpu, NumPy 2.5.4, running on `main` at `d936d0b`.

* Added `test_quantize_accepts_calibration_in_embedding_formats`, covering `int8` and `uint8` with the following input formats: regular tensors, `bfloat16` tensors, lists of vectors, lists of tensor vectors, lists of multi-vector matrices, and tensor-based `ranges`.
* Each test case compares dense, tensor, and multi-vector inputs against quantization using equivalent NumPy ranges.
* Before the fix: 8 failed, 4 passed.
* After the fix: 12 passed.
* Ran `pytest tests/util/test_quantization.py tests/util/test_similarity.py tests/util/test_tensor.py`: 350 passed, 20 skipped (CUDA-only and Windows-specific tests).
* Ran `pre-commit run` on the modified files: Ruff checks, Ruff formatting, and typos checks all passed.

Not tested:

* The full test suite.

title: [fix] Forward loading kwargs to nested SentenceTransformers in a Router
body:
Resolves #3822

## Problem
A `Router` whose routes hold whole `SentenceTransformer` models (e.g. `Router.for_query_document([st_q, Dense(...)], [st_d, Dense(...)])`) ignores the caller's loading kwargs once saved and reloaded:

```python
model = SentenceTransformer(path, device="cuda:1", model_kwargs={"dtype": torch.bfloat16})
```

- every nested model is first built on the default device (`cuda:0`) and only moved to `cuda:1` afterwards, which is the `cuda:0` allocation reported in the issue;
- `model_kwargs` (and `processor_kwargs`, `config_kwargs`, `backend`, `trust_remote_code`, Hub kwargs) are dropped, so the weights stay `float32`;
- `SentenceTransformer.load(...) is deprecated` is warned twice per route.

## Cause
`Router.load` calls `module_class.load(path, subfolder=..., **kwargs)` and falls back to `module_class.load(local_path)` on `TypeError`. For a nested model that is the deprecated `SentenceTransformer.load(input_path)`, which only takes one argument, so the first call always fails and the fallback runs `SentenceTransformer(local_path)` with no kwargs and no device. The top-level loader in `BaseModel` takes the same one-argument path for a `SentenceTransformer` listed directly in `modules.json`.

## Fix
`SentenceTransformer.load` now accepts the standard module loading kwargs. When a loader calls it with a `subfolder`, it resolves the subfolder with `load_dir_path` and builds the nested model on CPU with the forwarded kwargs (or with no `device` if `model_kwargs` has a `device_map`), leaving placement to the outer model like every other module. A direct `SentenceTransformer.load(path)` call behaves exactly as before, including the deprecation warning.

Both loaders are fixed by this one change; `Router.load` and `BaseModel._load_modules` are untouched.

## Validation
- New `test_router_load_forwards_kwargs_to_nested_sentence_transformers`: fails on `main` (`get_device_name` called twice), passes with the fix. It also checks `bfloat16` weights, no deprecation warning, and that the legacy direct call still warns.
- `pytest tests/base/modules/test_router.py tests/base/test_model.py tests/sentence_transformer/test_model.py`: 884 passed, 66 skipped.
- A `SentenceTransformer` nested directly in `modules.json` (not in a Router) now also loads in `bfloat16`, and encodes to the same shape.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: ruff check, ruff format, typos pass.

## AI assistance
I used an AI coding assistant to help trace the cause and draft the change; I reviewed and tested every line.

title: Respect per-call tokenization when excluding prompt tokens
body:
Prompt-excluding pooling can drop the first content token when a call disables special tokens through `processing_kwargs`. Transformer measured the prompt with instance settings and cached its length without the call's settings. This affects embedding workflows using `include_prompt=False` with per-call tokenization overrides.

Minimal reproducer (found through code analysis):
```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer(
    "sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-safetensors", device="cpu"
)
model.set_pooling_include_prompt(False)
output = model.encode(
    "Text one",
    prompt="query: ",
    output_value=None,
    processing_kwargs={"text": {"add_special_tokens": False}},
)
assert output["prompt_length"] == 2  # main reports 3 and excludes "Text" too
```

Measure the prompt with the call's settings and include effective processing settings in the cache key. Count real prompt tokens before excluding the trailing special token, so fixed-length padding is excluded on either side. Nested unhashable processor settings bypass caching.

Validated on macOS arm64, Python 3.13.15, PyTorch 2.15.0, Transformers 5.22.1, Sentence Transformers 6.3.0.dev0 (`a5d87ec`):
- `pytest tests/sentence_transformer/modules/test_pooling.py -q`: 255 passed, 156 skipped for unavailable accelerators. The 8 new encode-level regression cases cover `text`/`common` overrides, left/right padding, batch-longest/fixed-length padding, numerical pooling results, and restoring defaults. All four original override cases failed on unmodified main.
- `pytest tests/base/modules/test_transformer.py -k 'TestGetPromptLength or (TestPreprocess and test_preprocess)' -q`: 13 passed.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: Ruff check, Ruff format and typos passed.
- The reproducer, nested unhashable settings, and instance-setting cache isolation also passed. Tests used the cached tiny BERT fixture in offline mode. The full project and GPU/platform matrices were not run locally.
